Two clubs would be relegated as the league would be expanded to 12 teams for the 2006 season. Two teams promoted from the rival [[Provincial League]] and two clubs from [[Thailand Division 1 League]]. [[Thailand Tobacco Monopoly FC|Thailand Tobacco Monopoly]], who won the Premier League, beat league runners up [[Provincial Electricity Authority FC|Provincial Electricity Authority]] 4-1. ==Queens Cup== The [[Queen's Cup (football)|Queen's Cup]] was postponed because of lack of sponsorship, will be held next year but with reduced prize money. ==Asian Representation== * In the [[2005 AFC Champions League|2005 Asian Champions League]], a competition described as ''competition restricted to 14 countries considered 'mature' in the so-called 'Vision Asia' paper of AFC President Mohamed Bin Hammam. The so-called 14 'developing' countries have their clubs relegated to the AFC Cup, while the clubs from the 'emerging' countries are dumped into the new Presidents Cup.'' *[[BEC Tero Sasana]] and [[Krung Thai Bank FC|Krung Thai Bank]] would again be the Thai representatives and would also fail to qualify for the knockout stages. Krung Thai once again came in second place in their group, but a full 9 points behind group winners [[Busan I'Park]]. BEC would once again slump to bottom position on 1 point. *[[Thailand Tobacco Monopoly FC|Thailand Tobacco Monopoly]] took part in the 2nd edition of [[2005 ASEAN Club Championship|ASEAN Club Championship]] this season but failed to make it out of the group stage, drawing one game and losing the other two games. ==Annual awards== ===Coach of the Year=== *{{flagicon|Brazil}} [[Jose Alves Borges]] - [[Thailand Tobacco Monopoly FC|Thailand Tobacco Monopoly]] ===Player of the year=== *{{flagicon|Brazil}} [[Carlinhos Bala|José Carlos Da Silva]] - [[Thailand Tobacco Monopoly FC|Thailand Tobacco Monopoly]] ===Top scorer=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Supakit Jinajai]] - 10 Goals[[Football records in Thailand]] [[Provincial Electricity Authority FC|Provincial Electricity Authority]] *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Sarayoot Chaikamdee]] - 10 Goals[[Football records in Thailand]] [[Port Authority of Thailand FC|Port Authority of Thailand]] ==Champions== {{winners||Champions|[[TTM Chiangmai F.C.|Tobacco Monopoly]]|1st}} ==References== {{Reflist}} *[https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/thai05.html Thailand 2004/05] RSSSF ==External links== *[https://web.archive.org/web/20080913070725/http://www.thaifootballleague.com/ Official Website] {{S-start}} {{Succession box|title=[[Thai Premier League]]|before=[[2003–04 Thai League|Thai League
